name: Leicestershire
description: Leicestershire is a centrally located county in the East Midlands, combining productive farmland with a network of market towns. Leicester is the dominant urban centre, while the county is also known for its multicultural heritage, industrial history and association with the National Forest.

places.name: Melton
places.description: A rural district in Leicestershire centred on Melton Mowbray, famous as the home of the pork pie and a historic centre of Stilton cheese production.

places.name: Hinckley and Bosworth
places.description: A district in Leicestershire named for the market town of Hinckley and the site of the 1485 Battle of Bosworth Field, where Richard III was killed and the Tudor dynasty began.

places.name: Blaby
places.description: A small district in Leicestershire just southwest of Leicester city, largely suburban and semi-rural. Best known locally for Fosse Park, one of the region's largest retail and leisure parks.

places.name: Charnwood
places.description: A district in Leicestershire named for Charnwood Forest, an ancient upland landscape, and home to the university town of Loughborough.

places.name: Harborough
places.description: A rural district in Leicestershire around the market town of Market Harborough, known for its well-preserved Georgian high street.

places.name: Leicester
places.description: A historic city in the East Midlands where the remains of King Richard III were famously discovered beneath a car park in 2012. Home to significant Roman heritage sites and one of Britain's most diverse populations.

places.name: North West Leicestershire
places.description: A district covering former coalfield towns like Coalville alongside the National Forest, and home to East Midlands Airport.

places.name: Oadby and Wigston
places.description: A small suburban district on Leicester's southern edge, largely residential with a mix of Victorian terraces and green space.
